comments.text: The contrast between the endless golden desert dunes and the crystal-clear Persian Gulf coastline in Qatar is absolutely mesmerizing! Seeing an entire country thrive so beautifully surrounded by arid desert and ocean without a single river is mind-blowing. What a spectacular landscape!

comments.text: It’s absolutely wild that a country this wealthy has zero natural rivers. The fact that they were once only 48 hours away from running out of water is terrifying, but that $4 billion mega-reservoir project is a seriously impressive engineering feat.

comments.author: @giannisolga5191
comments.text: Having watched this video, I now realise that Iran's bombing Qatari desalination plants (July-August 2026) is not irritating, it is existential. Your explanation of the history of pearl fishing was wonderful. In the absense of bodies of water and therefore of grasslands and forests, hunting with falcons was not sport or a hobby, it was existential in terms of obtaining meat and protein. I look at rich sheikhs' placing such high value on falcons in a completely different context now. I thought of the introduction of desalination as a miracle, which it is. Your exposition teaches that it cannot go on forever. In the 80s Saudi Arabia seriously considered bring huge chunks of glacial ice from Greenland. It decided against it in the end. Because of climate change, even Greenland's glaciers are shrinking.  Will the skyscrapers one day lie in the desert like Ozymanias' statue?
